attributes.residual: After the retained change: insns 215/215, opcode multiset IDENTICAL, frame 88 and saved set (stmw r29) identical in both builds. The residual is now TWO items and its CLASS has changed, which is the real value of this pass. (1) A uniform FPR renaming - the whole function differs only in which FPR carries each value (e.g. target f8/f9/f0/f5/f4/f3 where ours has f5/f6/f7/f8/f3/f2). (2) ONE stack-slot delta: the `volatile f32 tmp` spill at enemy.c:4020 lives at 20(r1) in target and 64(r1) in ours (`lwz r0,20(r1)`/`stw r0,20(r1)` vs 64). BEFORE this pass the preheader ALSO disagreed on which VALUE occupied each load slot - target hoisted the two SDA21 constants lbl_803468B0/lbl_80346820 where ours hoisted the 56(r31)/60(r31) worldmat reads - i.e. the operands and their RELOCATIONS differed slot for slot. That is gone: every slot now loads the same value in both streams. WEBFRANK ASSESSMENT: still NOT eligible, but for a much smaller reason. Before the change the per-slot relocation payloads differed, which the guards forbid a postprocessor from hiding; now only the FPR names plus one stack displacement differ. Closing the single `tmp` slot would leave a pure renaming bisimulation and make this a genuine copy_register_fields pin candidate - that is the recommended next step, and it is a frame-LAYOUT question about what the fictional `u8 _pad15[48]` stands in for, not a register question.
